chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jameel, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'A man leaves his daughter, and his sister from his father and his mother.' So he said, 'The wealth, all of it, is for his daughter.'

key_terms.لِأَبِيهِ وَ أُمِّهِ: from his father and his mother (paternal and maternal sister)

ai.seo_question: Who inherits the entire estate when a man leaves behind both a daughter and a sister?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'blocking' (hijr) in Shia inheritance jurisprudence, where the presence of a closer heir (the daughter) excludes a more distant one (the sister). It highlights the specific scenario where the deceased leaves behind parents, yet the daughter still inherits the entire estate, demonstrating the precedence of direct descendants over ascendants and collaterals in this context. This ruling is foundational for understanding the distribution of the 'Fara'id' (fixed shares) versus 'Dhawi al-Arqab' (holders of the neck/primary heirs).
